chapter: Chicago cafes and the Browns band
title: Ray Lopez, the Windcliffe Inn and doubts about Ray Maxson
summary: Ray Lopez played at the Windcliffe Inn with singers and musicians around him; talk of Lopez as a top early trumpeter and whether Maxson was from New Orleans, whom Jernberg did not care for.

story.theme_name: Remembering the early trumpeters and their styles
story.community_name: Trumpeters I admired: rating the horn players

blocks.x: Salisbury were a singing trio in the Windcliffe Inn, and Ray Lopez was in the band that played for dancing down there. And Ray Lopez's father was the clarinet player. He could play the New Orleans style clarinet fairly well, you know, nothing to brag about. Ray Lopez, yeah. And Charlie Thorpe played piano there for the singers, and Earl, what the heck was his name, Earl Chigrew or some such name as that, played piano with the dance band. And then later on when Benny Fields married Blossom Sealy, Ray Lopez went with that act and played in the pit for where...
That's how they got... Well, what do you say about Ray Lopez being the best of the early Dixieland trumpet players is supported by, say, Frankie Quartel, for example. He swears by Lopez.
Yeah, I like Lopez. One thing that made me think that Ray Maxson was from New Orleans... I think he's a great guy. He might have. I'm pretty sure he... I thought they were a team, Fred. I think he's
from New Orleans. I'm pretty sure that he worked in New Orleans before... before he ever came to Chicago. But... Maxson could shoot the bull something awful... also. So...
To be very truthful with you, I never cared much for him. .
